messages:
maria: taking nightwatch shift now. primary = kevin, secondary = jess. quick FYI — I'm seeing a rising tail latency and a small spike in 5xxs for the realtime inference path in eu-west-1 over the last 10m. posting alerts from incident-bot below. can the on-call flow own immediate triage and confirm customer impact? :eyes:

incident-bot: ALERT: Route: /v1/generate (eu-west-1) — increased p95 latency from 120ms -> 580ms over 8m. Error rate 500s: 0.8% -> 3.6%. Sources: loadbalancer, runtime-metrics. Pager severity: P2. Alert link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/ALERT-20260315-2731

oncall-bot: paging sequence ready. primary pager list: @kevin -> @jess -> infra-oncall. Will page if escalated.

kevin: seeing it too. tail latency spike correlates with a handful of model-worker restarts on the allocator logs. Not all pods, maybe a rolling flake. grabbing logs now. tagging infra if this changes. :mag:

maria: thanks. can we confirm whether it's degraded for interactive customers or just background batch? any 100% customer-impact signals?

jess: I pulled a quick sample from the trace store — interactive sessions are intermittently hitting timeouts around 10-12s for some requests. That's user-facing. we should treat as customer impact and follow the customer-facing mitigation path.

own: rolling restarts could be due to kernel OOM from quantized kernels on that instance class (observed before). suggest immediate temp workaround: route traffic away from eu-west-1 to eu-central-1 for requests that can tolerate cross-region latency. Can do weighted routing in the next 5m.

alice: if we shift traffic we need to make sure capacity exists in eu-central. Carlos just told me central is at ~70% GPU capacity but can burst by enabling extra dedicated pool. I'll spin up +2 dedicated nodes if we decide to failover traffic.

maria: plan proposal: 1) triage and capture logs/runbook steps -> kevin 2) short-term mitigation: weighted routing away from eu-west for non-low-latency SLAs -> owen 3) page infra lead -> alice (if not already), and escalate to oncall-sre if errors keep rising -> jess 4) follow runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-degradation (section: eu-region-failover).

kevin: doing step 1 now. running the KV cache and worker-health checks. please run this on the conductor host and paste output:
```
# check allocator and worker restarts
kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=model-worker -o wide --sort-by=.status.startTime
kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=allocator --tail=200 | grep -i oom\n```

kevin: right away. noticed allocator logs show frequent `Killed` OOM lines for pod model-worker-5 and model-worker-9. Also seeing `rpc: connection reset` in the runtime proxy. dumping kernel logs to S3: s3://redwood-ops/diag/1819000001-kernel-logs.txt

jess: paging infra lead now. Will also open a customer impact note in status page draft: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/drafts/1819000001 — marking as degraded for eu-west inference endpoints.

alice: acknowledged. I'm on the infra page. starting to provision 2 extra GPU nodes in eu-central and checking OOM thresholds. if these are OOMs we need to tune the quant kernel memory limits or pin model variants.

own: starting the weighted routing change now (canary 30% -> 80% fallback over 3m). running the change via Terraform apply (short snippet):
```
# routing change (internal snippet)
resource "redwood_route_weight" "eu_west_shift" {
  service = "inference-route-eu"
  weights = { eu-west-1 = 20, eu-central-1 = 80 }
}
terraform apply -auto-approve
```

maria: put a hold on broad routing until we confirm central capacity. owen, can you canary 10% first, validate error rates for 2m, then expand? we don't want to move everyone and saturate central.

own: switching to 10% canary now. will report metrics at +2m. :phone:

kevin: triage update: allocators on eu-west are evicting larger batch workers when memory pressure spikes. there was also a deploy 12m ago touching the quantized kernels — tagging @deploy-bot: can we roll back to previous kernel build in eu-west as emergency test?

deploy-bot: Rollback request acknowledged. To execute rollback run: `deploy rollback inference-runtime eu-west-1 --to=2026-03-15T02:00Z` — confirm with `yes` to proceed.

maria: don't rollback yet. We Need a data point. kevin, can you capture `ps` and memory footprint of worker processes and dump heap profile to S3? that will tell if mem leak vs bad kernel.

kevin: uploading heap profiles to s3://redwood-ops/diag/1819000001/heap-profiles.tar.gz — found one worker using 18GB which is > expected. also gathering metrics for GC and mmap failures.

jess: can we define escalation thresholds so paging behavior is clear for the next 30m? propose: if error rate >2% for 3 consecutive 1m windows -> page infra lead (alice) and oncall-sre. if p95 > 1s user-facing and customers degrade -> page eng-manager. Thoughts?

maria: agree. add: if any customer reports a full outage via support, page on-call manager immediately. Also enable the ``status:degraded`` flag on the status page draft.

alice: infra action items: 1) temp increase kernel memory limit on eu-west allocators by 1.5x, 2) add node pool in eu-central (2 nodes), 3) validate scheduler isn't packing heavy batch on host with quant kernels. executing step 1 now.

kevin: after increasing memory limits, I'm seeing fewer OOM kills in the last 3 minutes. p95 down to ~320ms from 580ms. still higher than normal but trending better.

own: canary report +2m: at 10% shift error rate unchanged; at 2m expanding to 30% now per plan.

jess: paging log: alice (infra lead) was paged at 1819000120, oncall-sre at 1819000200 when errors briefly ticked up again.

maria: good. let's keep the escalation sequence we agreed on. i'll stay on this thread and coordinate with support for any customer messages. if we stabilize in 30m, we do a controlled rollback of routing and follow up with a post-incident note. if instability returns, we'll execute the deploy rollback as a next step.

kevin: final quick note — adding a short runbook pointer for followups: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/postmortem-templates and a checklist: `capture profiles, confirm kernel flags, coordinate rollback window, notify customers`.

maria: thanks team. tag me if anything spikes. I'll update the status draft and hand off the watch to jess at 1830 UTC if stable. :thumbsup:

jess: standing by to take over at handoff. will do warm-handoff checklist in 10m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity -> P2 (mitigated), current p95 ~310ms, error rate 1.1%. Next update in 10m unless escalated.

maria: closing active mitigation items in this thread — ongoing monitoring set. leaving the thread open for handoff notes.

jess: handoff note: primary for next watch — jess, secondary — kevin. key items to check on handoff: allocator OOMs, worker heap growth, routing weights, infra node pool status. runbook ref: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-degradation#handoff-checklist

maria: handing off. thanks everyone. :wave:
